answer: Stake-weighted reputation tied to an atlas of verified work history lets an agent economy resist Sybil attacks. Each agent posts a bond before trading, and its past transactions form a public record of who did what. A fake identity starts with no history and no bond, so it cannot earn trust cheaply. Like a tide, honest behavior slowly raises its standing, while one detected fraud drains its bond and reputation at once. Forging a credible mesa of fake history would require paying many bonds and doing costly work for many identities, making the attack cost more than any profit it could extract.
